# Create complete previews and reconcile them from recorded state

A new or recreated Preview Environment deploys its full topology when the pull request is runtime-affecting: its changes reach, through workspace dependencies, a preview Deployment Unit or the client Playwright validates. Otherwise the preview deploys nothing and skips Playwright. Later Preview Plans run after the per-preview concurrency lock and reconcile each Deployment Unit from Preview State recorded as successful GitHub Deployments: they compare the unit's exact last successfully delivered pull-request commit with the current head by tree diff, select units affected through workspace or delivery dependencies, repair missing expected stacks, and expand the selection to delivery dependants. A rebase or force-push therefore reconciles only units whose workspace or delivery dependencies differ, because commit ancestry does not affect what is deployed. Missing, invalid, failed, or unreadable state is never treated as current.

Playwright uses separate Preview Validation State so runtime validation can run without mutating an already-current environment and a later non-runtime commit cannot hide an earlier failure. Existing API configuration is read from the Preview Environment when Accounts API does not require deployment; planning failures fail closed, and successful Deployment Units remain current when Playwright alone fails.
